region: Pacific Northwest of North America, from Alaska to northern California
description: Western hemlock is a pale, even-textured softwood used for framing (often sold as hem-fir), joinery, mouldings, doors and plywood. It is unrelated to the poisonous hemlock plant (Conium).

hazards.summary: The UK HSE lists western hemlock dust as a cause of nose irritation (rhinitis) and effects on the airways. No primary study was found that confirms an allergy.
All wood dust is classified as carcinogenic to humans, mainly linked to cancers of the nose and sinuses. This applies to this wood like every other species.

related_species_note: The tree is not related to poison hemlock (Conium maculatum), a herb; health information about poison hemlock does not apply to this wood.
image_prompt: Photorealistic studio photograph of a freshly planed western hemlock (Tsuga heterophylla) board, shot at a low three-quarter angle so the face grain fills most of the frame. Pale creamy tan to light reddish-brown wood with a faint purplish-grey tint in places and little difference between heartwood and sapwood. Straight, even grain with moderately visible growth rings and a gentle earlywood-to-latewood transition, fine uniform texture, occasional thin dark mineral streaks, and a soft natural luster with no visible pores. Soft diffused daylight from upper left, gentle falloff, neutral warm-grey seamless background, shallow depth of field with the near edge tack-sharp. No text, no logos, no hands, no tools, no finish or varnish, natural unfinished wood. Wide 1200x630 composition (1.91:1) with the board centered and margin on both sides for cropping.
image_alt: Planed board of western hemlock with pale tan wood, straight grain and faint growth rings.
notes_internal: Botanical name verified on WFO as accepted Tsuga heterophylla (Raf.) Sarg. Only source is HSE-WIS30. PubMed searches for hemlock/Tsuga with sawmill, dust, asthma returned nothing relevant (results dominated by hemlock woolly adelgid and Conium).
